additional_unfalsifiable_assertions.finding: Both prefix output lists are collected before the divergent future samples are fed, so the test compares two identical clones on identical inputs. Deleting the divergent-sample lines leaves it green. It is a determinism check, not a causality check, and an encoder with a lookahead buffer would still pass.

The adversary block raises its own RuntimeError inside pytest.raises and exercises no production code; the test also contains no right-injection assertion despite its name. Shape coverage survives only through the separate monkeypatch test.
A bare pytest.raises(ValueError) accepts an unrelated 'empty training population' error, so deleting the whole-trajectory disjointness guard leaves the suite green.
assert_same_realization is called with one trajectory object repeated N times, so the pairing assertion can never fail at that call site even though the function itself is genuinely red-tested.

test_sc_deterministic_vs_residual_bias_separation_red and test_sc_gyro_oracle_retains_residual_bias_red are self-contained numpy arithmetic touching no production module; test_sc_learned_compensator_residual_bias_retention_red is a tautology because the correction head is zero-initialized, making the learned encoder bit-identical to the identity and its gradient exactly zero.
weak_axis_count and observable_plane_count are both assigned the total sample count, so the non-empty-population certificate cannot fail for any non-empty trajectory.

CF-1.satisfied_part: The forbidden-symbol vocabulary is genuine and recursive. Injecting each of A_m, b_m, C_BSm, A_g, c_g, C_SgB and their aliases/inverses is rejected, and disabling the rejection turns two tests red (M1b). No deployable path in the sealed code consumes truth, oracle, future samples, or any calibration symbol; the reproduced smoke confirms this at runtime.
CF-1.unsatisfied_part: The placement of the validator in the deployable path is not red-path protected. All three enforcement call sites can be deleted independently with the full suite green (M2b, M2c, M2d), because the only test that exercises the validator calls it directly rather than through the deployable entry points. The deployable/diagnostic variant guard is likewise unprotected: deployable_replay can be opened to the oracle variants N1 and C1 with the suite green (M29). The validator is also purely syntactic, so a forbidden quantity passed under a renamed key is undetectable by construction.

CF-2.satisfied_part: The normalization channel is genuinely protected: computing normalization from validation or test IDs turns test_sc_pairing_split_firewall_red red (M3, M15). validate_firewall enforces exact, non-empty, duplicate-free set equality and rejects any test-split intersection. In the sealed smoke, normalization sources equal the training ID set exactly, selection used validation only, and R4 never entered training or validation.
CF-2.unsatisfied_part: CF-2 explicitly requires the named test to become red on any test-split contribution to an early-stopping decision or checkpoint selection. It does not. Training loss and checkpoint selection can both be evaluated on the test split with all 42 tests green (M13, M14). Root cause: in train_variant the SplitFirewallRecord is constructed from the literals train_ids/val_ids rather than captured from the ID sequences actually consumed by _trajectory_epoch, so the declaration is decoupled from the executed data flow and validate_firewall becomes tautological for those three fields.

leakage_finding.evidence: Independent bit-exact reproduction of the smoke shows normalization_source_ids equal to the 16 training IDs, selection driven by the 8 validation IDs, R4 present only in the test split, and no oracle/truth/calibration symbol in any deployable namespace.
leakage_finding.note: The decision is FAIL_RED_PATH rather than FAIL_INFORMATION_LEAKAGE because no leakage exists in the sealed run and asserting one would itself be unsupported. This is not a downgrade: CF-1 and CF-2 remain NOT_SATISFIED and blocking, and the split firewall is currently a declaration that no test can falsify for the selection and training-loss channels.

equations_independently_re_derived_as_co: right-error definition q_true = q_hat (x) Exp(dtheta) with right multiplication injection and additive bias injection
reset covariance P+ = J_r(dtheta) P J_r(dtheta)^T using the correct SO(3) right Jacobian
error dynamics F[:3,:3] = -skew(omega), F[:3,3:] = -I consistent with the metric convention db = b_true - b_hat
magnetometer prediction h = C_BN(q_hat) m_N and Jacobian H[:, :3] = +skew(h), confirmed by an independent central finite-difference red path
Split gain K = G1 H^T G2 with shape 6x3 and split right/additive injection
deterministic compensation retains the stochastic residual gyro bias and the MEKF subtracts the estimated bias exactly once, with no double counting
unit and dt consistency throughout (rad, rad/s, dimensionless magnetic direction vectors, first dt = 0.1 s)
FiLM exact-off is a hard bypass, and branch isolation holds at factor level (gyro features -> G1 only, magnetometer features -> G2 only)
unverifiable_because_untested: the differentiable training unroll in study.py duplicates the entire recursion in torch and is never cross-checked against the numpy runtime operator; propagation sign, injection side, and innovation sign can each be inverted with the suite green (M22, M23, M24)
the backbone recurrent hidden state reset per trajectory (M20, M21)
the presence of the residual gyro bias in the generated sensor packet (M19)
contract_vs_code_divergences_non_blockin: C_SgB and C_BSm are fixed to identity and never applied by the forward generator, so every sensor-frame-to-body-frame statement in SC-00 is vacuously satisfied and corrected_B labels a sensor-frame vector; the config already declares identity_mounting_pilot_invariant: true, so restating SC-00 is the smaller correction
SC-00 places gyro/magnetometer noise after the scale matrix; the generator adds it before, so the recovered target carries untransformed noise
the SC-00 support constraint (singular values in [0.8,1.2], condition number <= 1.5) is never asserted in code
the initial G1 bias-attitude coupling has the opposite sign to the classical Riccati cross-covariance; it is trainable, so this is an initialization observation, not a math error

gate_decidability_finding.detail: evaluate_g1_gate consumes n2_r1_gyro_rate, n0_r1_gyro_rate, n2_r1_increment, n0_r1_increment, n2_r2_mag_angle and n0_r2_mag_angle, and evaluate_g4_gate consumes n3_divergence and n0_divergence. No function in the repository produces any of these arrays. The frozen divergence threshold ('evaluation','divergence_threshold_rad') = 1.0 is validated by load_config and then never read. The only implemented metrics are attitude geodesic RMSE and the weak-axis/observable-plane decomposition.
gate_decidability_finding.consequence: G1's three strict sensor sub-predicates and G4's no-added-divergence condition cannot be resolved by the sealed code. Deferring these producers to the experiment stage would require defining pre-registered metrics at the moment test access begins.
gate_decidability_finding.scope_note: The gate arithmetic itself matches canonical SC-01 and no threshold has drifted.

scope_findings.detail: Every gate constant, seed, population and architecture width is frozen in config and re-checked by load_config, which raises on any deviation. full_pilot_executed is false and no gate has been evaluated on test data, so post-hoc tuning has not occurred. The smoke emits no gate output and correctly carries performance_claim=false and physical_covariance_claim=false.
scope_findings.weak_axis_population_certificate: DEGENERATE: weak_axis_count and observable_plane_count are both set to the total sample count, so the non-empty-population certificate cannot fail for any non-empty trajectory.
